title: The Next Frontier | Mission Control
description:
# 🚀 Mission Control: Pitch Day

**Pitch your project. Win $1,000. ☄️**
Mission Control is the in-person pitch day of **The Next Frontier 2026**, a community-driven space innovation hackathon hosted by AI Collective Hampton Roads and presented by ECPI University.
Teams pitch their ideas in exploration, space medicine, space agriculture, or space tourism, and the top team takes home **$1,000**, announced at the end of the day.
Missed Friday's Launchpad workshop? You can still come. Pitch something you've been working on, cheer on the teams, or come see what Hampton Roads is building for space.
During Mission Control we'll:

* 🚀 **Pitch:** each team shares their idea and what they built
* 💡 **Get feedback** from judges and the community
* 🤝 **Meet** people who care about science, space, and AI
* 🏆 **Announce the $1,000 winner**

After pitch day, teams finish and submit their NASA project virtually on **Sunday, November 15**.
Friday night's workshop (Nov 13, 6–8 PM): [https://www.meetup.com/aicollectivehr/events/317121952/](https://www.meetup.com/aicollectivehr/events/317121952/)
📅 **Saturday, November 14, 2026**
🕚 **11:00 AM–2:00 PM EST**
📍 **ECPI University \| 5555 Greenwich Rd\, Virginia Beach\, VA**
🌐 **Event Website:** [https://aichr-nextfrontier.lovable.app/](https://aichr-nextfrontier.lovable.app/)
💬 **Discord:** [https://discord.gg/ecW2mY3DD](https://discord.gg/ecW2mY3DD)
✨ **No coding experience required. Beginners and curious minds welcome!**
**Pitch your idea. Win the mission. 🚀**

title: Seminar: Where Engineering Meets Cybersecurity:Skills That Bridge the OT Divide
description:
**Control systems are under constant threat, and patching and monitoring alone can’t stop an attacker who is determined and well resourced. Cyber-Informed Engineering (CIE) takes a different approach. It builds security into how systems are designed and operated, so the worst consequences can be engineered out.**

**Join Virginia “Ginger” Wright, CIE Program Manager at Idaho National Laboratory, for a session on what CIE looks like in practice. Ginger leads INL’s work on the DOE National Strategy for CIE and wrote the CIE Implementation Guide. She has also testified before the U.S. Senate on the subject.**
**You’ll leave with:**

* **A clear grounding in CIE. The session starts with a quick primer, so no background is needed.**
* **A current view of the threats to control systems. You’ll see what adversaries are doing now and why traditional defenses fall short.**
* **A real-world case study. It shows how CIE thinking changes outcomes.**
* **Hands-on knowledge of the tools for applying CIE. The main focus is how to use them, including the Engineering Controls Database.**

**Who should attend: ICS/OT security practitioners, control systems and process engineers, IT/OT convergence teams, asset owners and operators, security leaders, and anyone building a career in critical infrastructure protection.**

***Whether you’re an engineer learning security or a security professional learning engineering, this session gives you methods you can use right away.***

title: WSDG November Technical Presentation
description:
Detection and Notification Case Studies
by Glover Barker

Abstract:
An overview will be provided of three different domains in which a system is monitored for problems and the user is notified, and the user must respond. Commonalities and differences will be discussed. The domains are: Network Malware Filtering and Scanning, Airport Traffic Conflict Detection, and Intravenous Infiltration Monitoring.

Bio:
Glover Barker is a retired Software Architect. His background includes software development in C++, Python, and various other languages. He has also worked in management, requirements, design, testing, quality assurance, and configuration management. Past companies include ivWatch, NASA contractors, Symantec, R. R. Donnelley, Reuters, and AT&T Bell Laboratories.

title: AI Alien Alert! An Out-of-this-world app build night
description:
**👽 Your wildest idea could become your first app.**

​Join Tiffany and Howard for AI Alien Alert!—a social, hands-on build night where aliens, UFOs, and AI fuel your creativity.

​You’ll join a small crew, dream up an alien-inspired app, and use Lovable to bring it to life. Think UFO sighting trackers, alien matchmakers, or a guide to surviving first contact. Your team chooses the mission!

​No coding experience needed. We’ll demonstrate how to get started and help you along the way.

**​🚀 THE MISSION**

* Meet your crew and brainstorm an idea.
* Build your app prototype using AI.
* Take a break, mingle, and swap feedback.
* Refine your creation, then demo it to the room.
* ​You’ll leave with hands-on experience building with AI, new connections, and a playful prototype your team can keep exploring.

**​💻 COME PREPARED**
Bring a laptop and charger, and create a free account at lovable.dev before the event. Save your available build credits for the evening—we’ll share tips for making them count.

​Come solo or bring a friend. You don’t need a team or an idea beforehand—just curiosity and a willingness to experiment.

​🛸 Ready to join the mission? Register to reserve your spot!

​**[The AI Collective ](https://www.aicollective.com/?utm_source=luma)**is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 250,000+ leaders, builders, and stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, and coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress.

title: Code + Coffee | Cafe Stella
description:
Join us for a relaxed morning meetup where developers, designers, founders, and tech enthusiasts gather over great coffee to talk shop, share ideas, and connect with others in the local tech community.

**Code + Coffee** has no formal agenda—just bring your laptop, a project you’re working on, a question you’ve been thinking about, or simply come to meet other people building interesting things. Whether you're coding, designing, experimenting with AI, launching a startup, or just curious about technology, you'll find friendly conversations and plenty of inspiration.

Expect:

* Good coffee
* Interesting technical conversations
* People sharing projects and ideas
* Occasional spontaneous whiteboard sessions

Drop in anytime during the meetup window.

Stay for 10 minutes or the whole time.

If you’ve been looking for a low-key way to meet other developers in the area, this is it.

**Cafe Stella** has a policy that requires a purchase if you're sitting and staying in their space. Always a good idea to support the establishments we visit regardless.

title: Cybersecurity - Chesapeake Weekend Afternoon Networking (WAN)
description:
### **Moved to Tap It Local in Chesapeake**

## **Attention Information Security and Cybersecurity Professionals!**

Are you looking to meet new people who share your interests? Whether you're considering a career in cybersecurity, just getting started, or are a seasoned professional, we welcome everyone for an evening of networking, learning, and great conversation.

### **Why Attend?**

Join us at **Tap-It Local** in Chesapeake for a relaxed evening of networking with fellow IT and cybersecurity professionals. Connect with like-minded individuals, exchange ideas, and build lasting professional relationships. Whether you enjoy a cold beer or prefer something non-alcoholic, you'll find a welcoming community eager to share experiences and knowledge.
